**Horsehead Corporation: A Legacy of Innovation and Sustainability**  

Horsehead Corporation, headquartered at 300 Frankfort Road, Monaca, Pennsylvania 15061-2295, has emerged as a pivotal player in the chemical and metallurgical industries, specializing in the production of value-added zinc metal products and recycled materials. With a storied history dating back to 1943, the company was initially founded as a pioneer in zinc smelting, leveraging the abundant natural resources of the Ohio River Valley to support postwar industrial growth. Over the decades, Horsehead has evolved into a leader in sustainable metallurgy, focusing on recycling zinc from industrial byproducts such as electric arc furnace dust (EAFD), a hazardous waste generated by steel mills.  

The Monaca facility, strategically situated in Beaver County, PA, serves as a cornerstone of Horsehead’s operations, housing advanced processing plants that convert EAFD into high-purity zinc oxide and specialty alloys. These materials are critical for manufacturing in sectors ranging from construction to automotive, where zinc’s corrosion-resistant properties enhance product durability. In 2011, Horsehead was acquired by Umicore S.A., a Belgian materials technology group, further solidifying its global reach and commitment to eco-conscious innovation.  

A hallmark of Horsehead’s mission is its dedication to environmental stewardship. By transforming waste into valuable resources, the company not only reduces landfill contamination but also conserves finite natural reserves. Its operations adhere to rigorous environmental and safety standards, certified under ISO 14001 and ISO 9001 frameworks, ensuring quality and sustainability at every stage. Beyond industry impact, Horsehead actively partners with local communities near its Monaca plant to bolster economic development and STEM education initiatives.  

Today, Horsehead Corporation stands at the intersection of industrial expertise and environmental responsibility, poised to address the growing demand for recycled metals in a circular economy. For over 80 years, its legacy of innovation along Frankfort Road has underscored that responsible resource management and industrial progress can indeed coexist.
